title: Most Australian suburbs lack public transport frequent enough to make living without a car practical
oneLiner: Outside the inner ring, a car is not a choice.
body: Census journey-to-work data shows car use above 70 per cent in most middle and outer suburbs, and service frequency outside peak hours is low. In those areas the assumption behind removing minimums, that some residents will choose not to own a car, does not hold for most households.
contextBackground: This claim limits the geography of the proposal rather than opposing it outright: it suggests removal makes sense near frequent transit and little sense elsewhere, which is roughly what Auckland's experience showed.
contextDisagreement: The travel data is not disputed. Whether it argues for keeping minimums in those suburbs, or for letting developers there build parking anyway because buyers will demand it, is where the two sides part.

evidenceItems.citation: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Census of Population and Housing — method of travel to work by statistical area

otherClaim.title: Councils should abolish minimum parking requirements for new housing

claimItself.title: Councils should abolish minimum parking requirements for new housing
claimItself.oneLiner: Whether planning schemes should stop requiring a set number of car spaces per new dwelling and let builders decide.
claimItself.body: Most Australian planning schemes require new apartments and townhouses to include a minimum number of off-street car spaces, typically one or more per dwelling. The proposal removes the minimum. Developers could still build parking; they would no longer be required to.

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: Parking minimums add roughly $70,000 to the cost of a two-bedroom apartment in Sydney, $62,000 in Melbourne and up to $137,000 in Perth

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: Auckland removed minimum parking requirements citywide in 2016, and new developments near frequent transit have since provided markedly less parking

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: New housing completions have not kept pace with population growth in Australia's largest cities over the past decade

usedIn.relationSentence: This claim contradicts “Councils should abolish minimum parking requirements for new housing”
